$comment: Advisory customer-value estimates per feature spec (S16) — reach/impact/confidence are the authored values; score and tier derive from the calibration chart in specs/S16-feature-value-estimation.md. RICE is computed from specs/effort.json at report time and deliberately not stored here. Validated by npm run check:spec-value. NEVER read by the maturity scorer.

F01.justification: The namesake surface and a headline reason to install; gateway to F02, but its richest renderer wants Python on PATH, so the zero-setup path is the built-in fallback.
F01.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F02.justification: Everyone who opens the preview gets live refresh with no action; high polish per unit of user effort, but it only matters once F01 is in use.
F02.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F03.justification: Co-headline capability and the one that runs passively on every open file — the extension earns its keep here without the user asking.
F03.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F04.justification: Binding is the precondition that makes validation and preview point at the right schema; invisible when right, blocking when absent.
F04.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F05.justification: A form-based schema editor has no VS Code equivalent, but authoring schemas visually is a minority workflow next to reading and validating them.
F05.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F06.justification: Bootstrapping a schema from existing data removes an entire manual authoring session; used occasionally but decisively when it is.
F06.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F07.justification: Decisive for teams on private schema registries and irrelevant to everyone else — high impact inside a narrow workflow.
F07.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F08.justification: Invisible infrastructure that most users benefit from without knowing: faster repeat loads and offline resilience, with no configuration.
F08.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F09.justification: Settings are touched by a fair share of users but usually once, and the panel mostly saves a trip to settings.json rather than enabling anything new.
F09.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F10.justification: The `$schema` key is the idiomatic binding most JSON authors already write; honouring it means the extension works with no setup on files that already exist.
F10.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F11.justification: TOML schema validation is genuinely rare tooling, but TOML is a minority of the data files this extension sees.
F11.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F12.justification: SchemaStore auto-binding makes the extension do useful work on package.json, tsconfig.json and workflow files the user already has, with zero action — the widest no-effort reach in the set.
F12.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F13.justification: Go-to-definition across $ref turns multi-file schemas from a chore into navigation; matters most to the subset authoring large schemas.
F13.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F14.justification: Bundling is the publishing step for schema authors and runs in CI as well as the editor, but only authors who distribute schemas need it.
F14.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F15.justification: Breaking-change detection between schema versions is a capability few tools offer; its audience is schema owners with downstream consumers.
F15.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F16.justification: Sample data is a reliable time-saver for testing and documentation, though usually replaceable by hand-writing a short fixture.
F16.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F17.justification: Quality linting catches real schema smells for a substantial share of authors; advisory rather than blocking, so impact is moderate.
F17.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F18.justification: Schema-to-TypeScript removes a whole manual sync burden, but quicktype and json-schema-to-typescript already serve this need well outside the editor.
F18.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F19.justification: Completions and hover for TOML against a schema is unusual tooling, bounded by the same TOML minority as F11.
F19.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F20.justification: A workspace-wide report turns per-file validation into an auditable sweep, and the same answer is useful in CI.
F20.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F21.justification: Quick fixes convert F03 diagnostics from information into one-keystroke repair, offered automatically wherever validation already runs.
F21.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F22.justification: Draft migration is a rare but genuinely painful task to do by hand, and few tools automate the 07 ↔ 2019-09 ↔ 2020-12 moves.
F22.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F23.justification: An unused-in-data coverage report is the most speculative item in the set: the audience that would act on it is unclear, hence 0.5 confidence.
F23.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F24.justification: A dependency graph makes large schema sets legible, but it is a diagnostic people reach for occasionally rather than a daily surface.
F24.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F25.justification: Ranking enum suggestions by nearest match is a small, automatic delighter on top of F21 rather than a capability of its own.
F25.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F26.justification: A CI compatibility gate is decisive for the few teams that publish versioned schemas and invisible to everyone else.
F26.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F27.justification: The CLI takes the whole toolset outside VS Code into CI and scripting — a real differentiator, reaching the subset that automates schema work.
F27.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)

F28.justification: Editor-driven preview scroll keeps the panel showing whatever the author is currently editing, without hand-scrolling, and — when the position resolves — jumps to the exact matching section rather than an approximate one; a real navigation aid on a long schema, on by default, in the spirit of VS Code's own Markdown preview sync scrolling.
F28.estimator: the project's AI coding agent (Claude Code)
